name: Chiang Mai
summary: Golden temples in and around the moated Old City, Doi Suthep above town, khao soi and night markets, elephant sanctuaries and Doi Inthanon, Thailand's highest peak.

tips.title: Visa-free stays cut to 30 days
tips.body: From 15 September 2026 the 60-day visa exemption ended, and passport holders from 60 countries (including the UK, US and Australia) now get 30 days visa-free for tourism. Visa-free entries by land are generally limited to 2 per calendar year. Seychelles and Mauritius passport holders get 15 days, and visas on arrival apply to citizens of Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia.

tips.title: Show funds and an onward ticket
tips.body: Visa-exempt visitors may be asked for at least 10,000 baht per person or 20,000 baht per family, plus proof of onward or return travel. The visa-exempt entry covers tourism only, not business.

tips.title: Complete the TDAC within 3 days of arrival
tips.body: All foreign nationals have needed the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) since 1 May 2025. Submit it free in the 3 days before arrival at tdac.immigration.go.th.

tips.title: Vapes are illegal, including for tourists
tips.body: Possessing or using any vape, e-cigarette, pod, e-liquid or heat-not-burn device is illegal, with no exceptions for tourists. Penalties include confiscation, fines typically of 5,000–30,000 baht and detention. You may have to stay in Thailand until your case is finished.

tips.title: Cannabis is medical-only
tips.body: Recreational cannabis is illegal again. Use is allowed only with a Thai-issued prescription, limited to a 30-day supply. Taking cannabis out of Thailand without permission brings fines from 30,000 baht per kg and possible detention.

tips.title: Smoke haze in burning season
tips.body: Air pollution in Chiang Mai can reach dangerous levels during seasonal smoke from crop and forest burning. This can worsen asthma and sinus conditions. Wikipedia's Chiang Mai article puts the pollution season at roughly December to April and calls March the worst month.

tips.title: Dengue and other mosquito-borne diseases
tips.body: Dengue, Zika and malaria are risks in Thailand, and rabies is also present. Use repellent and get medical help for a high fever.

tips.title: Insurance and emergency numbers
tips.body: Hospitals require a guarantee of payment, so travel insurance is essential. Call 191 for police, fire or ambulance, or 1669 for an ambulance.

tips.title: Scooter rental needs the right licence
tips.body: Carry both a 1968 International Driving Permit (IDP) and your home licence, and wear a helmet, which is required by law. Driving without a valid licence can void your travel insurance.

tips.title: Never leave your passport as a deposit
tips.body: Don't hand over your passport as a guarantee to motorbike or other rental shops. They may hold it against claims for damage.

tips.title: Use ATMs inside banks
tips.body: ATM skimming has been reported, so use machines inside bank branches, cover your PIN and keep sight of your card.

tips.title: Respect the monarchy and mind what you post
tips.body: Criticising the Thai monarchy is a crime carrying long prison sentences, and the law is interpreted broadly. Posting photos online of people drinking or in clothing seen as inappropriate can also be illegal.
